title: Shadow Dribble
summary: One partner dribbles freely while the other copies every move with their own ball.
setup: Mark a 25 x 20 yard grid with 4 corner cones. Players in pairs, each with a ball. One is the leader, one is the shadow.
how: The leader dribbles anywhere in the grid, changing speed, direction and the part of the foot they use.
The shadow follows about 2 yards behind and copies everything the leader does.
Every 45 seconds the coach shouts 'Switch' and the roles swap.
Finish with one round where the leader adds a stop and a quick restart.
coaching: Small touches so the ball stays close
Eyes up to watch your partner and avoid other pairs
Leaders: mix slow and fast so the shadow has to react
easier: Walk-pace leaders only use inside and outside of the foot.
harder: Leader can call out a move (pull back, roll, cut) and the shadow must do it within 2 seconds.

title: Square Pass and Stretch
summary: Groups of four to five pass around a square, follow their pass, and add a movement prep exercise as they jog.
setup: Build a 15 x 15 yard square for each group. One player on each cone, with the extra player starting at the cone that has the ball.
how: Pass to the next cone to the right, then jog after your pass to that cone.
While jogging, do the movement the coach calls: high knees, side shuffle, open the gate, close the gate, backpedal.
After 2 minutes switch direction so the pass goes left.
Last round: two-touch only and sprint after your pass.
coaching: Open your hips to receive so you can play the next pass quickly
Pass with pace but keep it on the ground
Talk: call the name of the player you are passing to
easier: Make the square smaller and allow three touches.
harder: Add a second ball to the square starting at the opposite cone.

title: Ball Thieves
summary: Two thieves without a ball try to win one; anyone who loses a ball becomes the new thief.
setup: 30 x 25 yard grid. Everyone has a ball except two players in pinnies, who start outside the grid.
how: Players dribble around the grid keeping their ball safe.
On the whistle the two thieves enter and try to win a ball by stepping in and poking it away.
If you win a ball, keep it and dribble away. The player who lost it is now a thief.
Play 60 to 90 second rounds and count who never lost their ball.
coaching: Keep your body between the thief and the ball
Change direction away from pressure, not toward it
Thieves: stay on your feet and be patient before stepping in
easier: Only one thief, or thieves walk.
harder: Shrink the grid or add a third thief.

title: Triangle Pass and Follow
summary: Three lines on a triangle; pass, follow your pass, and add a wall pass once the rhythm is set.
setup: Place 3 cones in a triangle about 15 yards apart. Split 9-15 players into three lines. Two balls start with line A.
how: A passes to B and runs to the back of line B.
B receives on the back foot, passes on to C, and follows.
C passes back to A to keep the loop going.
Progression: A passes to B, B lays it back to A, then A plays a longer ball to C.
coaching: Receive with the foot farthest from the passer so you face the next target
Firm passes along the ground; follow through toward your target
Move off the cone a step before the ball arrives
easier: Allow three touches and shorten the sides to 10 yards.
harder: One-touch only, or reverse direction on the coach's call.

title: Gate Hunters
summary: Pairs move around the grid and score a point each time they pass through a gate to each other.
setup: Scatter 8 gates (2 cones, 2 yards apart) inside a 30 x 25 grid. Players in pairs with one ball.
how: Pairs dribble and pass around the grid looking for open gates.
A point counts when the ball goes through a gate and the partner controls it on the other side.
You cannot use the same gate twice in a row.
Play 60 second rounds; pairs try to beat their best score.
coaching: Inside of the foot, ankle locked, toe up
Look up to find the next free gate before you receive
Receiver: get in line with the gate and call for it
easier: Bigger gates (3 yards) and no time limit.
harder: Two-touch limit, or one pair becomes 'gate keepers' who stand in gates to block them.

title: Three-Zone Switch
summary: Keep the ball 4v2 in one end zone, then switch it over the middle zone to teammates waiting in the other end.
setup: Split a 40 x 25 area into three zones: two 15-yard end zones and a 10-yard middle. Four attackers in each end zone, two defenders start in one end zone.
how: Attackers in the zone with the defenders keep the ball and look to switch.
After at least 4 passes, play a pass along the ground through or across the middle zone to the far group.
When the ball is switched, the two defenders sprint over to press the new zone.
Defenders who win the ball swap with the two attackers who lost it.
coaching: Spread wide and deep to make passing lanes
Shift the ball to draw defenders, then switch quickly
Far group: get open early so the switch can be one pass
Weight the long pass so it arrives without bouncing
easier: Switch after 3 passes; only one defender presses.
harder: Switch must be first-time, or a third defender waits in the middle zone to intercept.

title: Touch Out of the Box
summary: A middle player receives inside a small box and must take the first touch out of a different side before passing on.
setup: A 4 x 4 yard box in the middle of a 20-yard channel. One server at each end, one worker in the box. Rotate every 90 seconds.
how: Server 1 passes into the worker in the box.
The worker's first touch must push the ball out of the box through a side the ball did not enter.
The worker then passes to Server 2 and steps back into the box.
Server 2 serves straight back in and the pattern repeats.
coaching: Check your shoulder before the ball arrives
Soft ankle, cushion the ball into space, not under your feet
Use the inside and outside of both feet
easier: Make the box bigger and let the worker stop the ball first.
harder: The coach calls 'left' or 'right' as the ball travels and the worker must touch out that side.

title: Turn Away From Pressure
summary: A receiver with a defender closing in uses the first touch to turn away and dribble through one of two gates.
setup: Server at one end. Receiver stands in the middle. A defender starts 5 yards behind the receiver. Two 3-yard gates on the far end line, one on each side.
how: Server passes to the receiver; the defender may move as soon as the pass is made.
The receiver reads which side the defender is coming from.
The first touch takes the ball away from that side and toward the open gate.
Receiver scores by dribbling through a gate. If the defender wins it, they try to pass back to the server.
Rotate: server to receiver, receiver to defender, defender to server.
coaching: Look over your shoulder before and while the ball travels
Open your body side-on so you can see the ball and the defender
First touch goes across your body and away from the defender, then accelerate
easier: Defender starts 8 yards away or only jogs.
harder: Add a third gate in the middle; defender may tackle from the first touch.

title: Pillow Catch
summary: Partners toss the ball by hand and the receiver brings it down softly with the foot or thigh, then passes it back.
setup: Pairs face each other 5 yards apart along a line of cones. One partner is the tosser with the ball in their hands.
how: Tosser lobs the ball underarm to the receiver's feet.
Receiver cushions it with the inside of the foot or the top of the foot so it drops dead, then passes back on the ground.
After 8 tosses, aim for the thigh: lift the knee, let the ball drop, then control with the foot.
Swap roles. Finish with a round where the receiver can use either surface.
coaching: Meet the ball early and pull the foot back as it lands, like catching an egg
Watch the ball all the way onto your foot
Relaxed body; stay on the balls of your feet
easier: Toss lower and allow the ball to bounce once first.
harder: Receiver must take the ball down and move it 2 yards to one side in a single touch.

title: Rush Hour
summary: Everyone dribbles in a busy grid and responds to the coach's traffic calls.
setup: 25 x 25 yard grid. Every player has a ball. The coach stands on the edge and calls out commands.
how: Players dribble around without bumping into anyone.
'Green light': dribble fast. 'Yellow light': slow, tiny touches. 'Red light': stop the ball with the sole.
'Roundabout': circle your ball using the sole. 'Reverse': pull the ball back and go the other way.
Anyone who touches another ball or player does 3 toe taps before carrying on.
coaching: Head up to find space
Use both feet and lots of small touches
Explode away after a change of direction
easier: Larger grid and fewer commands.
harder: Shrink the grid, or add a 'police car' player without a ball who tries to knock balls out.

title: Four Corner Escape
summary: Attackers dribble out of the middle and escape through any of four corner gates while defenders try to stop them.
setup: 25 x 25 grid with a 2-yard gate at each corner. Attackers with balls start in a centre circle of cones. Two or three defenders roam the grid.
how: On 'Go' attackers dribble out of the centre and try to get through any corner gate.
After escaping, dribble back around the outside and re-enter for another try.
Defenders stay on their feet and try to knock the ball out of the grid.
Count escapes in 90 seconds; rotate defenders each round.
coaching: Fake toward one gate, then go to another
Attack space early before defenders close it
Shield with your body when a defender gets close
easier: One defender, or make the gates bigger.
harder: Attackers must go through each corner once before any repeats.

title: Run It Into Space
summary: Players push the ball out in front with longer touches to dribble at speed into open space, then race a chasing defender to the end line.
setup: Two 40-yard channels side by side, each 10 yards wide. Attacker starts at one end with a ball. A defender starts on a cone 4 yards behind and to the side.
how: Attacker takes a big first touch forward and runs with the ball down the channel.
The defender chases when the attacker touches the ball.
Attacker scores by stopping the ball on the far end line before the defender catches up.
Jog back on the outside and swap roles.
coaching: Longer touches with the laces when there is space in front
Keep the ball slightly to the side so you can run in a straight line
Shorten your touches as you approach the line so you can stop it cleanly
easier: Defender starts farther back.
harder: Defender starts level, or attacker must finish with a pass into a minigoal at the end.

title: 1v1 Race to Goal
summary: An attacker receives facing a defender and tries to beat them and finish past the keeper.
setup: Goal with keeper on the top line. Attackers line up on the bottom line; defenders line up beside the goal post.
how: Defender passes the ball across to the attacker, then steps out to defend.
Attacker takes a positive first touch toward the defender and tries to beat them.
Attacker shoots once past the defender; play ends on a goal, save, or if the ball leaves the area.
If the defender wins it, they try to dribble over the bottom line.
Join the other line after each turn.
coaching: Attack the defender's front foot at speed
Use a fake or change of pace to unbalance them, then go
Shoot early once you create half a yard
easier: Defender must start from the goal line, giving the attacker more time.
harder: Five-second time limit to get a shot off.

title: End Line Breakout
summary: 1v1 in a narrow channel; the attacker scores by dribbling over the defender's end line under control.
setup: Narrow 20 x 12 channel. Attackers line up at one end with balls, defenders line up at the other end.
how: Defender passes to the attacker, then comes out to defend.
Attacker tries to stop the ball on the defender's end line for a point.
If the defender wins the ball, they score by passing it through the attacker's end line.
Each round lasts up to 20 seconds; then the next pair goes.
coaching: Run at the defender to make them stop and back up
Change direction or speed the moment they commit
Protect the ball with your body after you beat them
easier: Widen the channel to 15 yards.
harder: Attacker must get past within 3 touches of crossing halfway.

title: Pick a Goal 1v1
summary: Attacker faces one defender who guards two minigoals; the attacker chooses which one to attack.
setup: Two minigoals on the far line, one in each corner. Attackers start at the opposite end with balls. One defender starts between the goals.
how: Attacker dribbles at the defender.
Use fakes and body movement to shift the defender toward one goal, then attack the other.
Score by passing into either minigoal; no shots from more than 8 yards out.
Defender who wins the ball counterattacks to the attackers' start line. Swap after each go.
coaching: Show one way with your hips and eyes, go the other
Change of pace matters more than the trick
Pass into the goal with the inside of the foot once you are clear
easier: Defender must start on the goal line between the minigoals.
harder: Add a recovering second defender who starts 5 yards behind the attacker.

title: Shark Bay
summary: Fish dribble across the bay from one beach to the other while sharks try to kick their balls out; caught fish become seaweed.
setup: 30 x 20 yard bay with an end line beach on each side. All fish start on one beach with a ball. Two sharks without balls start in the middle.
how: On 'Swim!' all fish dribble across to the far beach.
Sharks try to knock balls out of the bay. A fish who loses their ball becomes seaweed.
Seaweed stands still where they were caught and can tag fish with their arms out, but cannot move their feet.
Keep crossing until only 2 or 3 fish remain; they are the next sharks.
coaching: Look for gaps between sharks before you go
Use a fake or a quick turn when a shark comes near
Sharks: stay on your feet and work together to close space
easier: One shark only.
harder: Fish must use their weaker foot only, or seaweed become extra sharks.

title: Cone Knockdown
summary: Two teams each guard five tall cones in their half and try to knock down the other team's cones with passes.
setup: Split the grid in half. Each team places 5 tall cones in their own half. Several balls start on the halfway line.
how: Players stay in their own half and pass the ball at the other team's cones.
Defend your cones by blocking with your feet or body (no hands).
A knocked-down cone stays down. First team to knock down all five wins.
Reset and play best of three, changing cone positions each round.
coaching: Use the inside of the foot for accuracy, laces for power
Move the ball sideways quickly to find a clear lane
Talk to teammates about which cone needs guarding
easier: Use more cones and bigger targets.
harder: Two-touch limit, or one player per team may cross halfway to retrieve balls.

title: Survival Cup
summary: Teams of two or three play together in one area; every team that scores is safe and steps off until the last team left is out.
setup: 35 x 30 yard area with a minigoal on each side. Make teams of 2 or 3 in different colours. One ball. Coach serves in from the side.
how: All teams play at the same time with one ball. Any team can score in any minigoal.
When a team scores, they step off and are safe for that round.
The last team that has not scored is out and does a fun challenge (juggling or passing target) on the side.
Keep playing rounds until one team wins the cup. Then everyone back in for a new tournament.
coaching: Work with your partner: one supports, one attacks
Shoot quickly; there are goals everywhere
When you lose the ball, win it back fast
easier: Use two balls so more players get touches.
harder: Goals only count from a one-touch finish or after a pass between teammates.

title: Square Rondo 5v2
summary: Five players on the outside of a small square keep the ball away from two defenders in the middle.
setup: Mark a 12 x 12 yard square. Five attackers spread around the edges, two defenders start inside. Run two squares side by side if you have more than 7 players.
how: Outside players pass around and across the square while the two defenders try to win the ball.
A pass that splits the two defenders counts as a point for the outside team.
If a defender touches the ball or it leaves the square, the player who made the mistake swaps in with the defender who has been in longest.
Play 60-90 second rounds and keep score of splits.
coaching: Open your body so you can see the next pass before the ball arrives
Move along your line to make a passing lane when a defender blocks you
Pass to the foot farthest from the defender
Look for the gap between the two defenders first, then go around them
easier: Make the square bigger or play 5v1.
harder: Limit outside players to two touches, or shrink the square to 10 x 10.

title: Two-Box Switch
summary: Keep the ball in one box, then switch it into the other box where teammates are waiting.
setup: Mark a 30 x 20 area split into two 15 x 20 boxes. Put 4 attackers in each box. Two defenders start in the box with the ball and one defender waits in the other box.
how: The four attackers in the ball box try to complete 5 passes against the two defenders.
After 5 passes they can switch the ball into the other box for a point.
Once the ball is switched, the two defenders who were pressing can send one player across to join the lone defender.
If defenders win the ball, they pass it to the coach and swap roles with the attackers who lost it.
coaching: Make the field big: get wide and deep in your box
Look up before the fifth pass so you know where the switch is going
Players in the far box move to get free before the switch arrives
Switch with a firm, flat pass along the ground
easier: Only one defender presses in the ball box.
harder: Switch after 3 passes but the switch must be a first-time pass.

title: End Zone Keep-Away
summary: Teams keep the ball and score by passing to a teammate who runs into the end zone.
setup: Mark a 35 x 25 area with a 4-yard end zone at each end. Two even teams of 4 or 5. Nobody may stand in an end zone; they can only run into it to receive.
how: Start with a coach pass to one team. Each team attacks one end zone.
Score a point by passing to a teammate who times a run into the end zone and controls the ball there.
After a point, the scoring team keeps the ball and attacks the other end zone.
If the defending team wins the ball, they attack right away.
coaching: Be patient: keep the ball until a runner is ready
Time your run so you arrive as the pass is played, not before
Pass into space in front of the runner
When you lose it, the nearest player presses straight away
easier: Allow a teammate to wait in the end zone, or add a free player who always plays for the team with the ball.
harder: Require 4 passes before a team can score.

title: Keeper Starts It (7v7)
summary: Keeper and three teammates play out from the back against two forwards, using the 7v7 build-out line.
setup: Use half of a 7v7 field. Mark the build-out line with cones (halfway between the top of the penalty area and the halfway line). Keeper plus 3 attackers start near goal; 2 defenders start on the far side of the build-out line. Two mini goals sit on the halfway line.
how: Keeper starts with the ball. The two defenders must stay behind the build-out line until the keeper passes or rolls it to a teammate.
Once the ball is played, the defenders can press anywhere.
Attackers score by passing into either mini goal or dribbling across the halfway line.
If defenders win the ball, they try to score in the big goal. Reset with the keeper after each goal or ball out.
coaching: Defenders split wide toward the sidelines to give the keeper options
Keeper, play to the side away from the closest forward
Receive with an open body so you can play forward
The midfielder moves into a gap between the two forwards
easier: Only one defender presses.
harder: Add a third defender who can press from the start; attackers must pass to the midfielder before scoring.

title: Back Three Build (9v9)
summary: Keeper, three defenders and two midfielders build out against four pressing players, respecting the 9v9 build-out line.
setup: Use half of a 9v9 field. Mark the build-out line with cones (halfway between the top of the penalty area and the halfway line). Keeper plus 5 attackers vs 4 defenders. Two mini goals on the halfway line.
how: Every restart begins with the keeper. Defenders stay on the far side of the build-out line until the keeper's pass is received.
Attackers try to pass or dribble into either mini goal.
Defenders who win the ball try to score in the big goal within 8 seconds.
After 4 minutes, rotate players through the back line and midfield roles.
coaching: Center back drops near the keeper; outside backs push wide and high
Play into the midfielder's back foot so they can turn forward
If the front is blocked, go back to the keeper and switch sides
Communicate early: call 'time' or 'man on' for the receiver
easier: Three defenders press instead of four.
harder: Remove the build-out line after the first round so forwards can press the keeper.

title: Through the First Line (11v11)
summary: A back four and two central midfielders play past three pressing forwards to find a target player in the end zone.
setup: Mark 60 x 45 from the goal line, with an 8-yard end zone at the far end. Keeper, back four and two central mids (team a) plus two targets in the end zone. Five defenders: three forwards and two midfielders. There is no build-out line at 11v11, so forwards may press the keeper.
how: Keeper starts each rep. Team a must get the ball to a target in the end zone for a point.
A point is worth double if the ball reaches a central midfielder who turns before the final pass.
Defenders who win the ball attack the big goal straight away.
Play 3-minute rounds; rotate the targets and mids.
coaching: Create a 3v2 or 4v3 against the forwards by dropping a midfielder or using the keeper
Hold the ball to draw a forward in, then pass past them
Center backs carry the ball forward when nobody steps to them
Midfielders check shoulders and position on the far side of the press
easier: Only the three forwards press; midfield defenders stay passive.
harder: Targets must receive with one touch and play back into a midfielder to finish the point.

title: Check, Turn and Shoot
summary: A striker checks toward a server, turns with the first touch and shoots before reaching the shooting line.
setup: Goal on the end line with a keeper. Server with balls about 22 yards out. Striker starts near the penalty spot. Two cones mark a shooting line about 12 yards from goal. Others wait in a line next to the server.
how: Striker checks toward the server, who passes along the ground.
Striker turns with the first touch, toward either side of the cones.
Striker shoots before passing the shooting line.
Striker becomes the server, server joins the line.
coaching: Look over your shoulder before the ball arrives so you know where to turn
First touch goes out of your feet and toward goal
Strike low and across the keeper
Follow your shot in for rebounds
easier: Striker starts facing goal and the server rolls the ball in front of them.
harder: Add a defender who starts behind the striker and pressures the turn.

title: Wide Runs and Cut-Backs
summary: Wingers dribble to the end line and pull the ball back low for two runners attacking the near post and the penalty spot.
setup: Goal with a keeper. A winger line on each side about 20 yards out. Two runner lines in the middle about 22 yards out. Cones mark the point where wingers must reach before passing.
how: Winger dribbles down the side past the cone toward the end line.
Two central runners go: one to the near post, one to the penalty spot.
Winger passes back low and hard across the box. Runners finish with one or two touches.
Alternate sides. Add one passive defender in the box once players get the timing.
coaching: Winger, look up before the pass and pick a runner
Runners, arrive late and fast rather than waiting in the box
Keep the delivery on the ground; finish with the inside of the foot
Near-post runner pulls the defender away for the second runner
easier: Winger stops the ball on the end line and passes from a standstill.
harder: Add an active defender and a recovering defender chasing the winger.

title: 2v1 to Goal
summary: Two attackers race at one defender and the keeper, deciding whether to dribble, pass or shoot.
setup: Goal with a keeper. Two attacker lines about 26 yards out, 10 yards apart. A defender line at the side of the goal.
how: Defender passes to either attacker line and steps out to defend.
The two attackers combine to score; aim to shoot within 8 seconds.
If the defender wins it, they try to dribble out over the start line.
Rotate: attackers go to the back of the other line, defender joins an attacker line.
coaching: Dribble at the defender to make them choose
If the defender steps to you, pass; if they hang back, keep going and shoot
Supporting attacker stays level or slightly behind the ball, not blocked by the defender
Shoot early when you have a clear sight of goal
easier: Defender starts farther away, giving attackers more time.
harder: Play 3v2 with a defender who recovers from behind.

title: Five-Second Counter
summary: A 4v4 game with keepers where a goal scored within five seconds of winning the ball counts double.
setup: Field 25 yards wide by 35 yards long with a goal and keeper at each end. Two teams of 4. Coach stands on the side with spare balls.
how: Play a normal 4v4 game.
When a team wins the ball, the coach counts out loud to five.
A goal scored before the count ends is worth 2; any other goal is worth 1.
Restart from the keeper after goals; coach plays a new ball in when it goes out.
coaching: When you win it, look forward first
Teammates sprint forward into space the moment the ball is won
First pass goes forward into a runner if it is on
If the counter is not on, keep the ball and build again
easier: Allow eight seconds for the bonus.
harder: The team that loses the ball scores a bonus point if it wins the ball back within five seconds.

title: Recovery Run 3v2+1
summary: Three attackers break on two defenders while a third defender sprints back from behind to help.
setup: Goal with a keeper. Mark a start zone about 20-30 yards from goal. Three attackers start in the zone with the coach. Two defenders wait near the edge of the box. A third defender starts behind the attackers.
how: Coach plays the ball to one of the three attackers.
Attackers go to goal straight away while the two defenders step up to slow them down.
The recovering defender sprints back on the goal side to make it 3v3 as fast as possible.
If defenders win the ball, they score by dribbling into the start zone. Rotate roles every few reps.
coaching: Recovering defender runs toward the goal first, not toward the ball
Front defenders delay: back off and keep the attackers in front
Attackers attack quickly before the extra defender gets back
Talk: recovering defender tells teammates which attacker to pick up
easier: Recovering defender starts closer to the goal.
harder: Two recovering defenders start behind, making it 3v4 if attackers are slow.

title: Lose It, Win It Back
summary: A 6v6 end-zone game where the team that loses the ball earns a bonus for winning it back fast.
setup: Field 35 wide by 45 long with a 5-yard end zone at each end. Two teams of 5-7. Coach on the side with balls.
how: Teams score by dribbling into the end zone they attack, or by passing to a teammate who runs onto the ball there.
When a team loses the ball, the coach counts to five out loud.
If that team wins the ball back before five, it earns a bonus point.
Play 4-minute games and change the bonus window as players improve.
coaching: Closest player presses the ball right away; others shut the nearby passing lanes
Press as a group, not one player alone
If you cannot win it in five seconds, drop back and get compact
Team with the ball: first pass away from the press, toward open space
easier: Use a seven-second window.
harder: Only one bonus point if you win it back in your attacking half of the field.

title: Jockey the Channel
summary: A defender passes to an attacker, closes down quickly and jockeys to stop them dribbling over the defender's line.
setup: Mark a 10 x 20 channel. Defender stands on one end line with the ball, attacker on the other end line. Set up several channels for larger groups.
how: Defender passes to the attacker and sprints out to close the distance.
As the attacker gets close, the defender slows down, gets low and jockeys.
Attacker scores by stopping the ball on the defender's end line. Defender scores by winning the ball and stopping it on the attacker's line.
Swap roles every rep; play 6 reps each.
coaching: Sprint while the ball travels, then slow down with short steps as you arrive
Arrive about an arm's length away, knees bent, weight on the balls of your feet
Stand side-on, not square, so you can turn and run with the attacker
Stay on your feet and be patient; poke the ball only on a heavy touch
easier: Make the channel narrower so the attacker has less room.
harder: Make the channel wider, or the attacker can score on either of two cone gates.

title: Curve and Show Outside
summary: Defenders use a curved approach to push the attacker away from the central mini goal and toward the wide gates.
setup: Mark a 20 x 20 square. Put a mini goal in the middle of one end line and a 3-yard cone gate in each corner of that line. Attackers start on the opposite line; defenders start beside the mini goal.
how: Defender passes to the attacker, then closes down.
Attacker scores 3 points through the mini goal or 1 point through either wide gate.
Defender earns 1 point for winning the ball, or for forcing the attacker out of the side of the square.
Swap roles after each rep; keep a running score.
coaching: Bend your run so you arrive on the inside of the attacker, blocking the middle
Show them the sideline with your body angle
Keep your feet moving; do not dive in or go to ground
Stay between the ball and the goal at all times
easier: Attacker must start with the ball stopped, giving the defender time.
harder: Defender must start from a cone 5 yards farther back.

title: Delay and Deny to Goal
summary: A 1v1 toward a real goal and keeper where the defender's job is to keep the attacker out of the central shooting zone.
setup: Goal with a keeper. Mark a central 'danger zone' in front of goal with cones. Attacker line about 27 yards out; defender line beside the post.
how: Defender passes out to the attacker and closes down quickly.
Attacker tries to score; defender tries to steer them wide and away from the danger zone.
Defender earns a point for winning the ball or forcing a shot from outside the danger zone.
Rotate lines after each rep.
coaching: Close quickly, then slow down and get low before you reach the attacker
Angle your approach to cut off the middle and send them wide
Stay on your feet; no slide tackles. Win the ball with a block or a poke when they push it too far
Work with the keeper: if you push them wide, the keeper covers the near post
easier: Attacker starts farther from goal, giving the defender more time.
harder: Attacker has a 6-second limit to shoot, forcing faster decisions from both players.

title: Four Mini-Goal Game
summary: A 4v4 game where each team defends two wide mini goals, so switching the point of attack pays off.
setup: Field 30 wide by 25 long. Place two mini goals near each corner on both end lines. Two teams of 4 or 5. No keepers.
how: Each team attacks the two mini goals on the opposite end line.
Score in either mini goal; restart from your own end line after a goal against.
Coach keeps balls ready and plays a new one in quickly when the ball goes out.
Play 4-minute games with short rests.
coaching: If one goal is crowded, switch quickly to the other
Spread out wide so the defenders have to cover more ground
Defenders shift together toward the side the ball is on
Look up after every touch to see which goal is open
easier: Make the field wider so goals are farther apart.
harder: A goal only counts if the team has used both halves of the field width in that attack.

title: Free Wings Game
summary: A 5v5 game with keepers and two side channels that defenders cannot enter, rewarding wide play and low crosses.
setup: Field 35 wide by 45 long with goals and keepers. Mark a 6-yard channel down each side. Two teams of 5 plus keepers.
how: Only one attacking player may enter a side channel at a time; defenders may not enter.
Players in a channel have three touches to pass or cross back into the middle.
A goal scored from a ball played out of a channel counts double.
Play two 8-minute halves; swap who plays in the channels.
coaching: Move the ball wide early to get it into the free channel
Central players make runs as the ball goes wide, near post and far post
Wide player: look up, then deliver low and hard across the goal
Defenders tuck in and protect the middle when the ball is wide
easier: Allow unlimited touches in the channel.
harder: One defender may enter the channel to press for a maximum of three seconds.

title: Build-Out Line Match (7v7)
summary: A full 7v7 match using build-out lines where every goal kick and keeper save must be played out on the ground.
setup: 7v7 field 40 wide by 55 long. Mark a build-out line at each end with cones, halfway between the top of the penalty area and the halfway line. Two teams of 6 plus keepers.
how: Play a normal 7v7 game.
On goal kicks and when the keeper holds the ball, opponents retreat behind the build-out line.
The keeper must restart with a pass or roll; no punts or long kicks.
Opponents may cross the build-out line once a teammate receives the restart. Award a bonus point for a goal that started with a keeper pass.
coaching: Spread wide quickly when your keeper gets the ball
Keeper, pick the open side and pass firmly
Forwards, wait behind the line and step up together when the ball is received
After receiving, look to play forward before playing back
easier: Opponents can only press once the ball crosses the build-out line.
harder: Bonus point only if the attack reaches the opponent's box in under 6 passes.

title: Set and Shuffle
summary: Keepers shuffle across the goal and get into a balanced set position just before each shot arrives.
setup: Put a cone 1 yard inside each post on the goal line and one cone 4 yards out from the middle of the goal. A server stands 10-11 yards out with a supply of balls. Extra keepers wait beside the goal.
how: The keeper starts at one post cone and shuffles sideways toward the other without crossing their feet.
When the server touches the ball out of their feet, the keeper stops, steps slightly forward toward the middle cone and gets set.
The server shoots at a catchable height to either side. The keeper catches or pushes the ball wide, then returns to the post cone.
Six shots, then rotate the next keeper in. Older keepers take a turn as server.
coaching: Feet about shoulder-width apart, weight on the front of the feet, knees soft
Hands relaxed in front of the body at waist height, palms toward the ball
Be still when the shooter's planting foot lands - not still moving
Keep the head steady and level so the eyes can track the ball
easier: Server rolls or throws the ball and the keeper starts already in the middle.
harder: Server uses fake shots and changes timing; the keeper must stay set and not guess.

title: Two Hands, Two Shapes
summary: Pairs practice the basket catch for balls at belly and chest height and the W catch for balls at face height and above.
setup: Pairs face each other 6-8 yards apart, each standing at a cone. The server holds the ball and the keeper starts in the set position.
how: Round 1: the server tosses underarm at belly height. The keeper scoops it with a basket catch and pulls it into the chest.
Round 2: the server tosses to face height. The keeper makes a W shape with thumbs and first fingers behind the ball and catches in front of the eyes.
Round 3: the server mixes high and low tosses without warning.
Ten serves per round, then swap jobs. Older pairs can serve with a side-foot volley from the hands.
coaching: Basket: little fingers close together, elbows tucked, trap the ball against the chest
W: thumbs almost touching, fingers spread and firm, catch out in front of the face
Take a small step toward the ball to meet it
Bring every catch back into the chest before letting go
easier: Stand closer, use a softer ball, and have the server say the catch type before tossing.
harder: Keeper starts facing away and turns on the server's shout; server strikes with the foot from 10 yards.

title: Dive Ladder: Sit, Kneel, Crouch, Stand
summary: Keepers learn to go to ground safely by starting low and moving up one level only when their landings are clean.
setup: Work in front of a goal on soft grass (use mats if the ground is hard). Put a target cone 3-4 yards to each side of the keeper. The server stands 5-6 yards away with the balls.
how: Sitting: the keeper sits with legs out and the server tosses to one side. The keeper falls sideways and catches with one hand behind the ball and one on top.
Kneeling: the keeper kneels upright and falls onto their side to make the catch.
Crouching: from a low squat the keeper takes a small step toward the ball and drops onto hip and shoulder.
Standing (older keepers): from the set position, step with the near foot and dive across toward the target cone.
Five serves to each side per level. Move up only when the keeper lands on their side, not on the belly or elbow.
coaching: Land on the side of the body: calf, thigh, hip, then shoulder
Hands lead the dive and the eyes stay on the ball
Pin the ball to the ground or pull it into the chest after landing
Step first with the foot nearest the ball - never fall backward
easier: Younger 7v7 keepers stay on the sitting and kneeling levels with rolled balls.
harder: Older keepers get a hip-height volley, then recover to the set position for a second save to the other side.

title: Keeper Distribution Targets
summary: The keeper picks the right delivery - roll, throw, punt or goal kick - to reach field players in near, middle and far zones.
setup: Keeper in goal at one end. Mark three zones going away from the goal: near (10-20 yards out), middle (20-30 yards) and far (30-40 yards). Put 2 field players in each zone and one field player beside the goal to serve balls in.
how: The server plays a ball into the keeper, who collects it.
The coach calls a zone. Near = roll along the ground, middle = overarm throw, far = punt or drop kick (or a goal kick from a placed ball).
The target player takes a first touch away from the nearest cone, then dribbles back to swap with the server.
After a few rounds add one defender in the near zone. The keeper must pick the open player and the right type of delivery.
coaching: Roll: step forward and stay low like bowling so the ball arrives flat to the receiver's front foot
Throw: turn side-on, bring the arm over the top and release toward where the receiver is running
Punt: drop the ball, don't toss it up; lock the ankle and strike through the middle of the ball
Look up before you collect so you already know where the ball is going
easier: Shorten the zones. Keep 7v7 keepers to rolls, throws and goal kicks, and only punt where your league allows it.
harder: Two defenders hunt the field players and the keeper has 6 seconds to release the ball.

title: Breakaway Battles
summary: An attacker breaks in on goal with a defender chasing, and the keeper times the approach to make a 1v1 save.
setup: Goal at one end. Attackers line up with balls at a cone 22 yards out; defenders line up 2 yards behind and to the side. Two cones about 10 yards out mark the keeper's working area, and a target cone sits out wide.
how: On the coach's call the attacker dribbles at goal and the defender chases to recover.
The keeper moves forward while the ball is away from the attacker's foot and gets set each time the attacker is about to touch it.
The keeper stays big and on their feet as long as possible, then goes low to block on the ball side. No head-first dives at feet.
If the keeper wins the ball, they roll or throw it to the wide target cone. If the defender wins it, they dribble out the side. Rotate lines after each go.
coaching: Close the gap on a heavy touch, stop and set on a light touch
Stay on the line between the ball and the middle of the goal
Make a wall: hands low and wide, body behind the hands
Lead with hands, arms and legs - never with the head
easier: Remove the chasing defender and start the attacker farther out so the keeper has time to set.
harder: Two attackers against one recovering defender; the keeper decides whether to come out or hold.

title: Press on the Trigger
summary: Defenders hold their shape and only jump to press together when a clear trigger happens.
setup: Big goal with a keeper at one end, two minigoals at the other. Team a (5 players plus the keeper) builds out from the big goal and attacks the minigoals. Team b (4 players) is the pressing team.
how: The keeper starts each rep by passing to a team a player.
Team b stays compact until it sees a trigger: a bad touch, a backward or square pass, the ball going to the sideline, or a receiver facing their own goal.
On a trigger the nearest player presses hard and the next players cut off the closest passes.
Team a scores by passing into either minigoal. Team b scores by winning the ball and finishing in the big goal within 8 seconds.
Play 2-minute rounds and swap roles every two rounds.
coaching: Shout the trigger ('Now!') so everyone goes together
Curve your run to shut one side and push play toward the sideline
Second and third defenders mark the nearest passes, not the ball
No trigger? Stay patient and compact - stay on your feet, no slide tackles
easier: Team a is limited to 3 touches and the coach calls the triggers out loud.
harder: Add a sixth player to team a; pressers have only 6 seconds to score after winning it.

title: Slide Together: Compact Block
summary: Six defenders move as one block across three channels so attackers can't find a gap through or between them.
setup: Goal with a keeper at one end. Split the area into three channels (left, middle, right) with cones. Six defenders (team b) set up in two lines of three. Five attackers (team a) start in the half away from goal.
how: Attackers move the ball side to side, looking for a pass through the block to a runner or a chance to shoot.
Defenders slide toward the ball together: all six must be in the ball's channel or the one next to it.
Keep the two lines no more than 10 yards apart. The coach freezes play when a gap opens and asks players to fix it.
Attackers score 1 for a shot on target and 2 for a pass received behind the back line. Defenders score 1 by winning the ball and passing it to the coach at the far end.
Play 3-minute rounds and swap roles.
coaching: When the ball travels, we travel - move while the pass is rolling
Squeeze the space between the lines and between teammates
Far-side players tuck in: give away the far side, never the middle
The player nearest the ball calls the shift
easier: Attackers must take three touches, giving defenders more time to slide.
harder: Attackers play two-touch and add a free player who only switches play.

title: Pressure, Cover, Balance
summary: Three defenders learn to share the jobs of pressure, cover and balance, swapping roles every time the ball moves.
setup: Goal with a keeper at one end. Two small cone gates (4 yards wide) in the far corners. Three defenders (team b) start near the goal; three attackers (team a) start at the far end. Extra players wait in lines.
how: The coach plays a ball to an attacker and the three defenders step out.
The nearest defender goes to the ball (pressure). The second sits a few yards behind and to the side (cover). The third tucks in on the far side to protect the middle (balance).
Each time the ball moves, the roles change: whoever is now nearest becomes pressure and the others adjust.
Attackers score in the goal. Defenders who win the ball score by passing through a corner gate.
Play until a goal or 45 seconds, then the next groups go.
coaching: Pressure: close quickly, slow down for the last steps, stand side-on and stay on your feet
Cover: close enough to help, far enough that one dribble doesn't beat you both
Balance: see the ball and the runner behind you
Talk: 'I've got ball!', 'I'm behind you!'
easier: Play 3v2 in the defenders' favor or limit attackers to 3 touches.
harder: Play 4v3 against the defenders so they have to stay compact and delay.

title: Claim It or Clear It
summary: The keeper and defenders handle balls from wide areas: the keeper claims what they can reach and defenders clear with the foot. No heading.
setup: Goal with a keeper at one end. Cones mark a small keeper area (6 yards out) and a larger box (14 yards out). An 8-yard wide channel on each side holds a crosser. Two attackers and three defenders start in the box.
how: A wide player dribbles down the channel and plays a low, driven cross toward the near post, the middle or the far post.
The keeper calls 'Keeper!' early and claims any ball they can reach in their area. Defenders protect the space in front of the keeper.
Defenders stay goal-side of the attackers, attack the ball and clear it with the foot toward the sideline. Crosses stay on the ground or below waist height - no heading.
Attackers score with any finish. Defenders score 1 for a clearance that goes out past the wide channel.
Alternate sides every cross. After 8 crosses, rotate attackers, defenders and crossers.
coaching: Keeper: decide early, call loudly, and catch the ball at the safest high point
Defenders: stay between your attacker and the goal, with eyes on ball and runner
Clear high, wide and far - toward the sideline, never across our goal
Near-post defender owns the first space; the far-side defender tucks in
easier: Coach serves crosses by hand, rolled or tossed low, from the edge of the channel.
harder: Add a third attacker making a late run. For 11v11 crosses can be lifted to the far post and the keeper must come and claim them; defenders still clear with the foot.

title: Set and Strike
summary: Shooters pass into a target player, get the ball laid back into their path and finish first time or with one touch.
setup: Goal with a keeper at one end. A target player stands at a cone about 12 yards from goal. Shooters line up with balls at a cone 22 yards out.
how: The first shooter passes firmly into the target player's feet and follows the pass.
The target lays the ball off softly to one side, into the shooter's path.
The shooter strikes first time or after one touch.
Shooter becomes the target, the target collects a ball and joins the line. Switch the lay-off side every few turns.
coaching: Pass firmly into the target and move straight away
Lay-off: soft, slightly to the side, into the path - not at the shooter's feet
Toe down, ankle locked, land on your shooting foot
Aim low and to the corners to make the keeper go down
easier: The target stops the ball dead for the shooter to strike.
harder: Add a passive defender behind the target; shooter must finish within two touches.

title: Wide Angle Finishing
summary: Players dribble in from a wide angle and shoot back across the keeper while a teammate attacks the far post for rebounds.
setup: Goal with a keeper at one end. A cone gate (2 yards wide) on each side about 10 yards from goal and 8-10 yards from the near post. One line of players with balls on each side, 20 yards out.
how: A player from the left line dribbles through the left gate and shoots.
As they go, the first player in the right line runs toward the far post to follow up any rebound.
Next turn starts from the right line, with a left-line runner to the far post.
Players switch lines after each turn so they finish with both feet.
coaching: Head up before the gate to see where the keeper is standing
Shoot back across the keeper toward the far post
Keep it low: it can be saved, deflected or tapped in by the runner
Far-post runner: time your run to arrive as the shot is struck
easier: Move the gates closer to the middle so the angle is wider.
harder: Add a recovering defender who starts beside the gate; shooters have 3 touches after the gate.

title: Rebound Hunters
summary: Two attackers take on one defender and the keeper, and every rebound is live, so players learn to follow every shot in.
setup: Goal with a keeper at one end. The coach stands at a cone in the middle 24 yards out with the balls. Attackers wait in pairs; defenders wait in a line beside the goal.
how: The coach passes to one of two attackers; one defender steps out from beside the goal.
Attackers try to score quickly. Whenever a shot is taken, the other attacker must follow it in toward goal.
Rebounds and parries stay in play until the keeper holds the ball, it goes out, or the defender clears it.
1 point for a goal, 2 points for a goal from a rebound. Next pair goes.
coaching: Shoot low and on target - it creates rebounds
Follow every shot, expecting the keeper to drop it
Rebound finishes: side-foot, calm, aim for the open space
Defender: stay on your feet and stay goal-side of the second attacker
easier: Remove the defender for 2v0 plus keeper.
harder: Add a second defender who joins from the end line 3 seconds later.

title: Triangle Turn and Play
players: 4 per triangle (set up as many triangles as needed)
summary: Players receive across their body on the back foot and play to the next cone, then follow their pass.
setup: Three cones in a triangle about 10 yards apart. Two players start at cone 1 with the ball; one player at each of the other cones.
how: Player 1 passes to cone 2 and follows the pass to take that spot.
The receiver at cone 2 opens up, takes the ball across the body with the back foot and passes to cone 3.
Keep the ball moving around the triangle. Every 2 minutes change direction.
Progression: receiver must take one touch to set and one to pass (two-touch), then one-touch when ready.
coaching: Open your hips so you can see where the next pass is going
Receive with the foot farthest from the ball
Pass with the inside of the foot, ankle locked, onto the receiver's front foot
Check away a step, then come to the cone to receive
easier: Make the triangle smaller and allow extra touches.
harder: Put a passive defender in the middle; the receiver must turn away from them.

title: Switch Through the Middle
summary: Keep the ball in one end grid, then switch it across the middle to teammates in the other end when the defenders are drawn in.
setup: Split the area into three 15-yard zones. Three attackers (team a) in each end grid. Two defenders (team b) start in the end grid with the ball; one defender patrols the middle zone.
how: The ball starts with the three attackers in one end grid; the two defenders press them.
After at least 3 passes, attackers may switch the ball through the middle zone to the other end grid.
The middle defender tries to cut out the switch. The two pressing defenders run across to press in the new grid.
Attackers score 1 point for each successful switch. If defenders win it, they pass to the coach and get a point.
Play 3-minute rounds and rotate defenders.
coaching: Draw the defenders in with short passes, then switch
The player switching needs a first touch out of their feet to open the long pass
Receivers spread wide and make an angle the middle defender can't block
Weight the switch so it arrives on the ground or at an easy height
easier: Remove the middle defender, or allow the switch after 2 passes.
harder: Two-touch limit and the switch must be first time after the third pass.

title: Find the Third Player
summary: A short pass into a target and a lay-off free a third player's pass into the run of the first player.
setup: Player 1 starts at a cone at the bottom with a ball. Player 2 stands about 10 yards ahead with their back to the far end. Player 3 supports 5 yards to the side. Player 4 waits at a cone gate at the far end.
how: Player 1 passes into player 2's feet.
Player 2 lays the ball back to player 3.
As soon as the first pass is played, player 1 runs forward past player 2. Player 3 passes into that run.
Player 1 receives on the move and passes to player 4 at the gate. Everyone moves up one spot and player 4 starts the next rep from the bottom.
coaching: Player 1: pass and go - your run starts as the ball leaves your foot
Player 2: one touch, soft lay-off to the side, don't turn
Player 3: open up early so you can see the runner before the ball arrives
Pass in front of the runner so they don't have to stop
easier: Allow two touches for each player and walk through the pattern first.
harder: Add a defender behind player 2 who can step to intercept; the group chooses third-player pass or turn.

title: Movement Lanes
equipment: 1 ball per player for the last round
summary: Players warm up in lanes with a new movement each trip, building to short bursts and a dribble.
setup: Set up 3-4 lanes, each marked by a start cone and an end cone about 12 yards apart. Split players evenly behind the start cones.
how: First trip: easy jog to the end cone and back.
Each trip adds a movement out and a jog back: high knees, side shuffle (face each way), skips for height, backward jog looking over the shoulder, hip swings (open and close the gate).
Bursts: half pace to the middle, three quick steps, then speed up for the last few yards.
Final trip with a ball: dribble out with inside and outside touches, turn at the end cone and dribble back.
coaching: Stand tall and let the arms work with the legs
Quality first, then build the speed
Land quietly on the front of the foot
Stay in your lane and leave space for the player ahead
easier: Fewer movements and more jogging; young players copy a leader at the front.
harder: Add reaction calls: on the coach's clap, turn and sprint back to the start.

title: Wake-Up Rondo 5v2
summary: Five players around a square keep the ball from two defenders in the middle to get touches and brains switched on.
setup: Mark a 12 x 12 yard square. Five players spread around the outside edges; two defenders in pinnies stand in the middle.
how: Outside players pass to keep the ball away from the two defenders. They can slide along their side but not step into the middle.
If a defender touches the ball or it leaves the square, the player who made the mistake swaps with the defender who has been in the middle longest.
Ten passes in a row earns the outside group a point.
Play 2-minute rounds with a short stretch between rounds.
coaching: Open your body so you can see the next pass before the ball arrives
Pass to the foot farthest from the defender
Defenders work as a pair: one presses, one blocks the pass between them
Move along your side to make an angle for the player on the ball
easier: Play 6v2, or 4v1 for younger groups, and allow three touches.
harder: Two-touch, then one-touch; a pass split between the defenders counts double.

title: Dribble Tag Traffic
summary: Everyone dribbles inside a square while two or three taggers try to tag them; frozen players are freed by a teammate.
setup: Mark a 25 x 25 yard square. Every player has a ball except 2-3 taggers, who carry a pinny in their hand.
how: Dribblers keep their ball moving inside the square. Taggers try to tag them with a gentle touch on the back or shoulder - no pushing.
A tagged player freezes and holds their ball above their head.
A teammate frees them by dribbling a full circle around them.
Play 60-90 second rounds and change taggers each round. Count how many players are frozen at the end.
coaching: Small touches so the ball stays close when you change direction
Head up: look for space and for frozen teammates
Use turns and changes of speed to escape
Use the whole square, not just the middle
easier: One tagger, and dribblers can pick up the ball for a 3-second safe spot on a cone.
harder: Taggers also dribble a ball; the square shrinks each round.

title: 4v4 Four Mini Goals
summary: Two teams of four each defend two mini goals and attack two, so players learn to spot the open side and switch play.
setup: Mark a 40 x 30 yard field. Put two mini goals on each end line, about 8 yards in from each corner. Two teams of 4, no keepers. Spare balls sit beside each goal.
how: Play 4v4. Each team attacks the two mini goals on the far end line and defends the two on its own line.
A goal counts when the ball is passed or shot into either mini goal from inside the field.
After a goal or a ball out of play, the coach sends a new ball to the team that conceded.
Play 3-minute games with a 1-minute water and talk break, then swap pinnies or change matchups.
coaching: If one goal is crowded, look up and switch to the other one
Spread out wide so the defense has to cover the whole width
Defenders: the nearest player presses, the others cover the goal behind
Shoot early once the lane to a goal opens
easier: Play 4v2 or 4v3 for short spells so attackers find more open space.
harder: A goal only counts if the team switched the ball from one side of the field to the other during that attack.

title: Three-Zone Build and Score
summary: A conditioned game on a field split into thirds where teams must connect a pass in the middle zone before they can attack the final third.
setup: Mark a 36 x 54 yard field with a goal on each end line. Split the length into three 18-yard zones with cones. Two teams of 5 to 7 plus keepers.
how: Play a normal game with keepers, starting each restart from the keeper.
Before a team can enter its attacking third, it must complete at least one pass to a teammate standing in the middle zone.
A goal is worth 1 point. It is worth 2 if every outfield player on the scoring team is past the halfway point of the field when the ball goes in.
If a team enters the final third without the middle-zone pass, the ball goes to the other keeper.
Play 5-minute games and give a short coaching stop between each.
coaching: Middle players: check away, then come toward the ball to get free
Receive on the half turn so you can see forward
Back players: step up as the ball moves forward to earn the 2-point bonus
When you lose it, the nearest two players squeeze the ball right away
easier: Allow a pass or a dribble into the middle zone to unlock the final third.
harder: Two-touch limit in the middle zone, and the defending team may drop one extra player into its own third.

title: End-Zone Touchdown Game
summary: Teams score by getting the ball under control inside the end zone, which rewards forward runs and well-timed passes.
setup: Mark a 30 x 45 yard field with a 5-yard end zone at each end. Two teams of 4 to 6. No goals and no keepers.
how: Each team attacks one end zone and defends the other.
Score a point by dribbling into the end zone and stopping the ball with your sole, or by receiving a pass inside the end zone and controlling it.
Defenders may not stand inside their own end zone; they can only chase in after the ball.
After a point, the scoring team gives the ball to the other team, who restart from their own end zone.
Play 4-minute rounds and track points across rounds.
coaching: Time your run into the end zone so you arrive as the pass arrives
Passer: play the ball into space in front of the runner
If no run is on, keep the ball and move it to the other side
Defenders: track runners instead of watching the ball
easier: Make the end zones 8 yards deep or add a neutral player who always attacks.
harder: Points only count from a pass into the end zone, not a dribble.

title: 4v3 Overload to Goal
summary: Four attackers try to use their extra player to score past three defenders and a keeper; defenders who win the ball counter into two mini goals.
setup: Mark a 40 x 35 yard area with a goal and keeper on the top line and two mini goals on the bottom line. Place a cone line 7 yards in from the bottom as the attackers' start line. 4 attackers, 3 defenders, plus a keeper. Extra players wait by the start line.
how: The coach plays a ball to any attacker on the start line, and the 4v3 begins.
Attackers try to score in the big goal within 30 seconds.
If a defender or the keeper wins the ball, the defending team tries to score in either mini goal.
Attackers get 1 point per goal; defenders get 1 point per counter goal or per stop that ends in a ball out of play.
Rotate one attacker and one defender out after each rep so everyone plays both roles.
coaching: Make the field big: two wide attackers stay near the sidelines
Dribble at a defender to pull them, then release the free player
Shoot as soon as you see the goal between defenders
Defenders: stay compact, protect the middle, delay until help arrives
easier: Play 4v2 plus keeper.
harder: Attackers must score within 15 seconds, or play 5v4 with a two-touch limit.

title: Pirates and Treasure
summary: Everyone dribbles their own treasure while two pirates try to knock balls out of the grid; lost treasure is repaired at the dock.
setup: Mark a 25 x 25 yard grid with a small 6 x 6 yard repair dock in one corner. Every player has a ball except two pirates in pinnies.
how: Players dribble anywhere in the grid, keeping their ball close.
Pirates try to steal or poke balls out of the grid. They may not use hands or slide.
A player who loses their ball collects it, goes to the repair dock, does 10 toe taps, then rejoins.
Every 60 seconds, the coach picks two new pirates. Play 6 to 8 rounds.
coaching: Keep your eyes up so you can see where the pirates are
Use your body to shield when a pirate gets close
Change speed and direction to get away
easier: Start with one pirate who must walk.
harder: Add a third pirate, or players must use only their weaker foot.

title: Flip It
summary: Two teams race with the ball at their feet to flip cones up or down; the team with more cones their way when the whistle blows wins.
setup: Scatter 16 to 20 cones in a 30 x 25 yard grid, half standing up and half turned upside down. Two teams, each player with a ball. One team are Uppers, the other Downers.
how: On go, players dribble to any cone, stop the ball with the sole, then flip the cone their team's way with one hand.
A player may not flip the same cone twice in a row, and nobody may guard or stand over a cone.
After 60 seconds the coach blows the whistle; count up and down cones to find the winner.
Play 5 or 6 rounds, swapping roles each time.
coaching: Short touches as you get near the cone so you can stop fast
Look up to find the nearest cone that needs flipping
Keep the ball close while you flip so nobody knocks it away
easier: Players can leave their ball and run to cones for the first round.
harder: Flip only after doing a turn around the cone, or use the weaker foot only.

title: Bank Robbers
summary: Four small teams race to dribble balls out of the center bank and back to their corner, then raid each other's corners.
setup: Mark a 30 x 30 yard grid with a 6 x 6 yard home base in each corner and a 6 x 6 yard bank in the middle filled with balls. Split players into four teams, one per corner.
how: On go, one player at a time from each team runs to the bank, dribbles a ball back, and stops it inside their home base. Then the next teammate goes.
Balls must be dribbled, never thrown or kicked long. Hands are not allowed.
Once the bank is empty, players may take balls from any other team's home base. Nobody may block or guard their own base.
After 90 seconds, the team with the most balls wins the round. Reset and play 5 or 6 rounds.
coaching: Small touches when you get close to the base so the ball stops inside
Pick the target with the most balls and the fewest players nearby
Big touch to escape, then close control
easier: Two players per team can go at once.
harder: Must do a turn before leaving the bank, or dribble with the weaker foot only.

title: Turn and Go Lanes
summary: Players dribble up a lane, perform a called turn at the far cone, and burst back to the start.
setup: Set up 4 lanes, 5 yards apart, each with a start cone and a turn cone 13 yards away. 2 to 4 players per lane, each with a ball.
how: The first player in each lane dribbles at a steady pace to the turn cone.
Just before the cone, they perform the turn the coach calls: inside hook, outside hook, sole drag, or step-over turn.
After the turn, they speed up and dribble back past the start cone, and the next player goes.
Change the turn every 2 minutes and finish with a race round where players pick their own turn.
coaching: Slow down a step before the turn, then explode out of it
Lower your body and keep the ball close as you turn
Look up after the turn before you speed away
Practice turns with both feet
easier: Walk through each turn first, then jog.
harder: Put a passive defender behind the turn cone who steps forward after the turn.

title: Beat the Line 1v1
summary: In narrow channels, an attacker tries to dribble past a defender and stop the ball on the far line.
setup: Make three side-by-side channels, each 10 yards wide and 15 yards long. In each channel, attackers line up at one end, defenders at the other with the balls.
how: The defender passes the ball to the attacker, then steps forward to defend.
The attacker tries to dribble past and stop the ball with the sole on the defender's end line.
If the defender wins the ball, they can score by dribbling over the attacker's line.
Players join the back of the opposite line after each rep. Each rep lasts up to 15 seconds.
coaching: Attack the defender with speed, then change pace to get past
Use a fake or a body swerve to move the defender off balance
Push the ball past them and accelerate into the space
Defenders stay on your feet, no diving in or sliding
easier: Make the channel wider, or the defender starts further away.
harder: Narrow the channel to 7 yards, or add a 5-second limit to beat the line.

title: Rush Hour Corners
summary: The whole team dribbles in heavy traffic around a no-go box and races through corner gates when the coach calls a number.
setup: Mark a 30 x 30 yard grid with a 10 x 10 yard no-go box in the middle and a cone gate across each corner. Number the gates 1 to 4. Every player has a ball.
how: Players dribble around the grid without entering the no-go box.
When the coach calls a gate number, everyone speed dribbles through that gate, then returns to free dribbling.
Last three players through the gate do 5 quick sole rolls before rejoining.
After a few rounds, add two defenders who try to win balls; anyone who loses a ball swaps in as a defender.
coaching: Head up so you can find space and avoid crashes
Little touches in traffic, bigger touches in open space
Use the outside of the foot to change direction quickly
easier: Make the no-go box smaller and leave out defenders.
harder: Call two numbers, and players must go through both gates in order.

title: Diamond Receive and Turn
summary: Players pass around a diamond, receiving on the half turn so their first touch sets up the next pass.
setup: Place 4 cones in a diamond, about 11 yards from cone to cone. One player at each cone, with two at the start cone and the ball.
how: The start player passes to the next cone and follows the pass to take that spot.
The receiver opens their body, takes the first touch across their body toward the next cone, and passes on.
Keep the ball moving all the way round the diamond. Change direction every 2 minutes.
Add a second ball once the group is passing cleanly.
coaching: Open your hips before the ball arrives so you can see the next target
Receive with the back foot, the one furthest from the ball
First touch goes where you want to pass next, not under your feet
Check away, then step toward the ball as it comes
easier: Allow three touches and shorten the distance.
harder: Two touches max, or the coach calls left or right to set the next pass direction late.

title: Called Gate First Touch
summary: In pairs, the receiver must move the ball with the first touch through the gate the server calls.
setup: Pairs stand 12 yards apart. Behind the receiver, set two small gates, 2 yards wide, one off each shoulder about 4 yards away.
how: The server passes to the receiver and calls 'left' or 'right' as the ball travels.
The receiver's first touch must push the ball toward the called gate, then a second touch carries it through.
The receiver turns, dribbles back to the middle, and passes back to the server.
Swap roles every 8 passes.
coaching: Stay on your toes so you can react to the call
Use the inside or outside of the foot to angle the touch
Touch it into space, not too far, so the next touch is easy
easier: Call the gate before the pass is played.
harder: Server calls later, or the receiver must use only one touch to get the ball into the gate.

title: Touch Away From Pressure
summary: A receiver with a defender closing from behind must read the pressure and take the first touch into the open side to score in a mini goal.
setup: Mark a 20 x 25 yard area with two mini goals on the top line. A server with balls stands at the bottom. The receiver starts in the middle. A defender starts at a cone near the top.
how: The server passes to the receiver. The defender can leave the cone as soon as the pass is played.
The receiver checks over a shoulder, takes the first touch away from the defender, and tries to score in either mini goal.
If the defender wins the ball, they pass it back to the server for a point.
Rotate server to receiver to defender to server every rep.
coaching: Look over your shoulder before the ball arrives
Touch it to the side the defender is not coming from
Use your body between the defender and the ball
If the defender is tight, cushion it with your chest or thigh first on a lofted serve, then turn
easier: Defender waits until the receiver's first touch before moving.
harder: Server mixes in lofted serves, or add a second defender from the side.

title: Five-Second Win-Back
summary: A small-sided game where a team earns a bonus point for winning the ball back within five seconds of losing it.
setup: Mark a 35 x 45 yard field with a goal and keeper at each end. Two teams of 5 or 6. The coach stands on the sideline with spare balls and counts out loud.
how: Play a normal game with keepers.
When a team loses the ball, the coach counts to five out loud.
If the team that lost it wins it back before the count ends, they get 1 bonus point.
A goal is 2 points. A goal scored within 5 seconds of a win-back is worth 3.
Play 4-minute games with short breaks.
coaching: Closest player sprints at the ball the moment it is lost
Next two players cut off the easy passes nearby
If you cannot win it fast, drop back and get organized
Team in possession: get the ball away from the pressure quickly
easier: Make it a 7-second count.
harder: Bonus point only if the ball is won back in the attacking half.

title: 3v2 Back-and-Forth Waves
summary: Three attack two toward one goal; as soon as the rep ends, the two defenders plus a teammate attack the other way, so players switch roles constantly.
setup: Mark a 30 x 40 yard field with a goal and keeper at each end. Two teams. Each team has two defenders waiting near its own goal and the rest lined up at the halfway point on the sideline.
how: Three red attackers dribble in and play 3v2 against two blue defenders toward the top goal.
When the attack ends (goal, save, or ball out), the two blue defenders plus one blue player from the sideline attack the bottom goal right away.
Two red players wait near the bottom goal to defend that wave. The coach plays a new ball in if needed.
The three players who just attacked step off to the sideline; keep the waves going for 3-minute rounds and count goals.
coaching: Attackers: spread out so one defender cannot mark two players
Draw a defender with the dribble, then pass to the free player
Defenders: the first one delays, the second covers the pass
On a turnover, think attack straight away
easier: Play 3v1 waves.
harder: Attackers have 8 seconds to score, or make it 4v3 waves.

title: Win It and Break Out
summary: Attackers go at a goal while defenders who win the ball must break out quickly through one of three counter gates.
setup: Use half a field, 50 yards wide and 40 yards deep, with a goal and keeper on the top line. Set three 4-yard cone gates near the bottom line. Five attackers against five defenders plus the keeper.
how: The coach serves a ball to the attackers, who try to score in the goal.
When the defenders or keeper win the ball, they have 8 seconds to dribble it through any counter gate for a point.
Attackers who lose the ball try to win it back before it reaches a gate.
Play 4-minute rounds, then swap the teams' roles.
coaching: Defenders: first pass after winning it goes forward if you can
Players away from the ball sprint wide and forward to give options
Carry the ball into space with big touches when nobody is in front
Attackers: react straight away when you lose it
easier: Give the defenders 12 seconds and four gates.
harder: Defenders must pass through the gate to a teammate instead of dribbling, and only have 6 seconds.

title: 4v2 Split-Pass Box
summary: Four players on the outside of a small box keep the ball from two defenders inside, with a bonus for passes that split them.
setup: Mark a 12 x 12 yard box. Four attackers stand on the sides, one per side. Two defenders start inside. Spare balls by a corner.
how: Attackers move along their side line and pass to keep the ball away from the defenders.
Count passes out loud. Ten passes in a row is a point, and a pass that goes between the two defenders counts as two.
If a defender touches the ball or it leaves the box, the attacker who made the mistake swaps in with the defender who has been in longest.
Play 90-second rounds and keep personal points.
coaching: Slide along your line to open a passing lane for the player on the ball
Pass to the foot further from the defender
Look for the gap between the two defenders before you receive
Defenders: work together so one presses and one blocks the middle
easier: Make the box 15 x 15 or play 4v1.
harder: Two-touch limit, or shrink the box to 10 x 10.

title: Keep It and Switch
summary: Two teams play keep-away with two neutral helpers, earning a point for six passes in a row and double if they switch the ball from one wide channel to the other.
setup: Mark a 40 x 35 yard area with a 5-yard wide channel down each side. Two teams of 5 plus 2 neutral players (marked N) who always play with the team in possession.
how: The team with the ball tries to complete 6 passes in a row, using the neutrals as needed.
6 passes earns 1 point. If those passes include the ball going from one wide channel to the other, it earns 2.
Only one player from each team may stand in a wide channel at a time.
When the other team wins the ball, they start their own count. Play 4-minute rounds.
coaching: Make the field big with width and depth when your team has the ball
If one side is crowded, move it quickly to the other side
Body open to see both sides before you receive
Defenders: shift together as a group toward the ball
easier: Point for 5 passes, and add a third neutral.
harder: Neutrals get one touch, or the switch must happen in three passes or fewer.

title: Passing in 3s: Check, Shoulder, Turn
summary: Dynamic movement, then passing in threes where the middle player checks, looks over her shoulder and receives facing forward.
setup: 4 minutes of dynamic movement first (jog, high knees, butt kicks, side shuffles, carioca, short sprints). Then groups of three in a line, 10-12 yards apart, one ball per group.
how: The end player passes to the middle player, who checks toward the ball.
Before the ball arrives the middle player glances over her shoulder.
She receives on her back foot, opens up to face the far player and passes on.
The passer follows her pass and becomes the new middle player.
coaching: Look before it gets to you
Open your hips so you can see the field
First touch away from pressure and toward where you're going
This is the center mid's movement in the build-out
easier: The middle player can take two touches and doesn't have to turn on the first touch.
harder: The coach calls 'man on' as the ball travels: the middle player must play it straight back instead of turning.

title: Build Out Through the Center Back and Center Mid
summary: The keeper, back three and center mid build out against three pressers and score through gates on the halfway line.
setup: Half field. Keeper plus left back, center back, right back and center mid against 3 pressers (2 forwards and a mid). Three small cone gates across the halfway line.
how: The keeper starts every ball.
The building team scores by passing or dribbling through a gate on the halfway line.
The pressing team scores by winning the ball and shooting on the big goal.
First 8 minutes: the center mid must touch the ball before it goes through a gate.
Then add a fourth presser who marks the center mid.
coaching: Center mid: show in the space ahead of the center back, never right next to her
Center mid: if a defender is between you and the ball, move into a passing lane
Center mid: check your shoulder and turn forward when you can; if not, play back or wide and show again
Center back: split wide of the keeper with the fullbacks spread out
Center back: no pressure? Dribble forward into midfield to pull a defender and free a teammate
Center back looks in order: center mid's feet, the wide back, a ball into space for a forward
Center back: when the ball goes wide, stay central and slightly behind; talk and direct
Lose it: center back gets goal-side and delays instead of diving in
easier: Start with 2 pressers, or let the building team use a 6th player (a wide mid).
harder: Add the 4th presser on the center mid from the start, or give the builders 10 seconds to reach a gate.

title: Balls Into Space: End Zone Game
summary: 4v4 plus 2 neutrals. A goal only counts when a teammate runs onto a pass into the end zone.
setup: 40 x 30 yard grid with a 5-yard end zone at each end. Two teams of 4, plus 2 neutral players who play for whoever has the ball.
how: Each team attacks one end zone.
A goal counts only when a teammate runs into the end zone and receives a pass there.
Passes to a player already standing in the end zone don't count.
After a goal, the scoring team keeps the ball and attacks the other end.
Progression: a goal scored within 3 passes counts double.
coaching: Pass to where she's going, not where she is
Runner: go before the pass, at an angle, and point to where you want it
Pass firm enough that the defender can't cut it out
Look for the run early; don't wait until it's covered
easier: Make the grid wider, or add a third neutral player.
harder: Two-touch limit, or the runner must finish with one touch into a mini goal at the back of the end zone.

title: Finishing Through Balls
space: Final third with a full goal
summary: A passer slides a through ball between two cones; the forward times a curved run, takes one touch toward goal and finishes.
setup: Keeper in a full goal. A line of passers at the top (center mids get extra turns) and a line of forwards near the sideline about 30 yards out. A cone gate about 22 yards out stands in for the defense.
how: The passer plays the ball through the cone gate.
The forward times a curved run so she stays onside and meets the ball moving forward.
One touch toward goal, then shoot.
Swap lines after each turn.
Last 6 minutes: a defender starts 3 yards behind the forward and chases.
coaching: Run so the ball comes to you moving forward; don't stop and wait
First touch out in front of you, toward goal
Shoot early, before the keeper sets
Low and across the keeper to the far post
Passer: weight it so the forward doesn't have to break stride
easier: No chasing defender, and the forward can take two touches.
harder: Start the chasing defender level with the forward, or add a recovering center back in front of the gate.

title: Scrimmage With Build-Out and Through-Ball Rules
summary: A full scrimmage against another team, with rules for the first 15 minutes that reward building out and through balls.
setup: Full field, 9v9 against the visiting team. Normal restarts except as below.
how: First 15 minutes: every goal kick is played short to the center back or a fullback, no long kicks.
First 15 minutes: a goal scored from a through ball counts double.
After that, play normally.
Coaches give quick sideline comments; don't stop play.
coaching: Center mid: show and turn when the keeper has it
Center back: dribble forward into midfield when no one presses you
Forwards: time your runs so you're onside and moving onto the ball
Shoot early once you're through
easier: Allow the keeper to roll the ball out to anyone on goal kicks.
harder: Keep the build-out rule for the whole scrimmage, or require 3 passes in your own half before crossing midfield.
